target.title: RFC: OpenShell session workers and local inference
target.body:
## Summary

Proposes a plugin-gated OpenShell worker provider for OpenClaw. Each dispatched session placement owns a disposable OpenShell sandbox while the long-lived OpenClaw Gateway remains outside. Workers use the existing Gateway inference proxy by default or an optional credential-free `inference.local` route whose provider credential remains in the OpenShell Gateway.

## Motivation

The NemoClaw-style topology places one whole OpenClaw Gateway inside one OpenShell sandbox. That gives the Gateway a single containment boundary, but it does not provide independently disposable sandboxes for individual OpenClaw sessions. OpenClaw's existing cloud-worker lifecycle already supplies durable per-session placement, fencing, transcript ownership, workspace reconciliation, and reclaim semantics.

This RFC reuses those semantics instead of nesting the OpenShell sandbox backend or exporting OpenShell-managed secrets into OpenClaw.

## Proposed contract

- Register `openshell` as a worker provider only when `@openclaw/openshell-sandbox` is installed and enabled.
- Map each OpenClaw worker placement to one deterministic OpenShell sandbox.
- Keep direct SSH host-key pinning unchanged while adding a bounded provider-authenticated SSH `ProxyCommand` transport.
- Keep Gateway-proxy inference as the default.
- Allow a worker provider to advertise an immutable, credential-free local-inference route with exact provider/model admission.
- Negotiate local inference through `worker-local-inference-v1`; older workers retain Gateway-proxy behavior.
- Persist the route with the lease and clear it with the lease.
- Document OpenShell's current one-provider/model route per Gateway limitation, including no in-session switching or fallback.

## Implementation alignment

The companion [`sallyom/openclaw:openshell-session-workers`](https://github.com/sallyom/openclaw/tree/openshell-session-workers) branch implements this RFC's current scope:

- plugin-owned OpenShell provisioning, inspection, deletion, and `inference get` validation;
- generic core contracts for provider-authenticated SSH and worker-local inference;
- durable route persistence and immutability;
- launch-time provider/model enforcement and protocol negotiation;
- worker-side Anthropic/OpenAI SDK routing through `inference.local`; and
- documentation that the integration exists only when the OpenShell plugin is enabled.

The RFC intentionally does not include browser login or a broader credential-broker design.

## Tradeoffs

- Local inference moves provider routing and credential injection from OpenClaw to OpenShell.
- One OpenShell Gateway currently exposes one selected provider/model pair to all local-inference workers.
- Route drift is checked during provisioning or deterministic adoption, not on every turn.
- The plugin currently parses human-readable `openshell inference get` output.
- The generic transport, persisted route, protocol feature, and worker runtime path add core surface even though OpenShell policy remains plugin-owned.

## Validation

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` in the RFC repository.
- Companion implementation: 188 focused tests, core production/test typechecks, OpenShell plugin typecheck, plugin SDK surface check, full build, and a clean fresh autoreview.
- Manual setup has verified that OpenShell stores the Anthropic credential, validates `openclaw-anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`, and exposes that selection as `inference.local` without giving the credential to OpenClaw.

The RFC remains `draft`; `issue` stays blank until acceptance.

<!-- agent-transcript:start -->
## Agent Transcript

<details>
<summary>Redacted Codex collaboration summary</summary>

```text
[user]
Investigate whether OpenShell provider and credential management can combine with the OpenClaw OpenShell sandbox plugin.

[assistant]
Established the security boundary: the existing sandbox backend can mediate credentials for tools inside a sandbox, but host-side OpenClaw model calls do not traverse OpenShell. Rejected exporting OpenShell credentials through an OpenClaw SecretRef; the safe seam is mediated use, not secret extraction.

[user]
Would an OpenShell worker provider give sandboxed LLM interaction and individual sandboxes per agent/session, unlike the one-lump NemoClaw design?

[assistant]
Separated the two requirements. A worker provider places the agent loop and tools inside a per-session environment. Worker-local `inference.local` routing additionally makes model egress originate inside that same OpenShell sandbox. OpenClaw's placement invariant attaches at most one session to an environment.

[user]
Would starting OpenClaw inside OpenShell and enabling the sandbox plugin create nested OpenShell sandboxes? Is this proposal the same idea without nesting?

[assistant]
Confirmed the distinction. The proposed Gateway remains outside OpenShell; the plugin provisions one sandbox directly for each worker placement. The restricted worker runtime does not load general plugins, so it does not recursively activate the sandbox backend.

[user]
Can OpenShell CLI providers, credentials, and inference.local carry through OpenClaw? What is the switching limitation?

[assistant]
Defined a fixed placement route: OpenShell owns the provider record and credential, while OpenClaw stores only a credential-free base URL plus the expected OpenClaw provider/model. OpenShell currently exposes one user inference route per Gateway, so in-session provider/model switching and fallback are rejected.

[user]
Write this as a narrowly scoped OpenClaw RFC and implement the OpenShell-as-is version. Keep browser login and unrelated future credential-broker work out of RFC 0020.

[assistant]
Produced RFC 0020 and the companion implementation. The plugin registers both independent capabilities when enabled: `SandboxBackend` keeps the agent loop on the Gateway and redirects tools, while `WorkerProvider` places the agent loop and tools in a disposable OpenShell sandbox. Core changes remain provider-neutral.

[proof]
The implementation branch adds deterministic OpenShell worker leases, provider-authenticated SSH, immutable local-inference persistence, worker protocol negotiation, exact route admission, worker-side local inference, focused tests, docs, typechecks, SDK surface validation, full build validation, and clean autoreview.
```

</details>
<!-- agent-transcript:end -->
